speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you've presented with gait and limb ataxia along with a significant medical history; to begin our assessment, could you please describe the specific symptoms you are experiencing and how long they have been present? Additionally, have you noticed any issues with your vision, hearing, or coordination when walking?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a distinct imbalance on the right side. Given your history of significant medical issues, have you ever suffered a stroke, had a spinal cord injury, or undergone any major surgeries? Also, have you noticed any changes in your vision or hearing?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy for Crohn's disease.

*Note: While PML is the primary concern given the ataxia and immunosuppressive history, a final confirmation requires neuroimaging. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain with and without contrast. REQUEST TEST: JC Virus Antibody Status (CSF).*
